name: Tenet
blurb: Nolan's spy thriller about an agent fighting a future war waged by objects moving backward
title: Tenet Explained: Plot Summary and Ending
description: Tenet explained: who is who, inversion and turnstiles, the full plot from Kyiv to Stalsk-12, and the ending explained step by step.
h1: Tenet Explained: Plot, Inversion and Ending
answer: Tenet is a 2020 spy thriller written and directed by Christopher Nolan, starring John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki and Kenneth Branagh. A CIA agent known only as the Protagonist is recruited by a secret organisation after a mission in Kyiv goes wrong. He learns that people in the future have found a way to reverse the direction of time for objects and people, called inversion, and are sending things back into the present. With the help of a handler named Neil, he has to stop a Russian oligarch who is in contact with the future and preparing something far worse than a nuclear war.

head: Character
Who they are
rows: A CIA operative recruited into a secret organisation called Tenet
A British agent who becomes the Protagonist's handler and partner
A Russian oligarch and arms dealer who communicates with the future
An art appraiser and Sator's estranged wife, trapped in the marriage by a forged painting and their son
An arms dealer in Mumbai who works for Tenet
A British intelligence officer who points the Protagonist to Priya
A scientist who explains inverted objects to the Protagonist

body.note: Key terms. Inversion: reversing an object's or person's entropy so it moves backward through time; an inverted bullet flies back into the gun. Turnstile: a machine that inverts whoever walks through it. Inverted people must carry oxygen, because ordinary air does not pass through their lungs. The Algorithm: a nine-part device from the future that could invert the entire world, destroying the past.

body: Beginning. During a staged terrorist siege at the Kyiv opera house, the Protagonist joins a CIA extraction. A masked soldier with an orange trinket on his bag saves his life with a bullet that seems to travel backward. The Protagonist is captured and tortured, and bites a suicide pill, which turns out to be fake: it was a test of loyalty, and he is the only one to pass it. He wakes to learn he has been recruited into Tenet, a group fighting a war against the future. A scientist, Barbara, shows him inverted bullets, which are caught by a gun rather than fired from it. Tracing them, he meets Neil, and together they reach Priya Singh in Mumbai. She tells them the bullets were inverted for Andrei Sator, who is somehow in contact with the future.

Middle. Sir Michael Crosby advises the Protagonist to approach Sator through his wife Kat, who once authenticated a forged Goya painting for Sator. He now uses the forgery to blackmail her and control access to their son Max. The Protagonist promises to free her by stealing the painting from a freeport warehouse at Oslo airport. During the break-in, he fights a masked man who has stepped out of a turnstile; the fight has no clear winner. Through Kat, the Protagonist gets close to Sator on his yacht in Italy and offers to help him steal a case of plutonium in Tallinn. In the heist, an inverted Sator ambushes them on the highway, takes the case, which is actually a piece of the Algorithm, and shoots Kat with an inverted bullet. To save her, the Protagonist, Neil and Kat go through Sator's turnstile and travel backward in time to the Oslo freeport. On the way, the Protagonist realises that the masked man he fought at the freeport was his own inverted self.

In Oslo, Priya explains that Sator now holds all nine pieces of the Algorithm. She had let him take the last piece so that he would reveal where the rest were hidden. Kat tells them that Sator has terminal cancer. Rather than die alone, he means to end the world: on the day he kills himself, during a family holiday in Vietnam, a switch tied to his pulse will send the Algorithm's hiding place to the future, and the future will trigger it. The Algorithm is buried in Sator's abandoned hometown, Stalsk-12, in Siberia.

End. Tenet launches a 'temporal pincer': one team moves forward in time, another inverted team moves backward through the same ten minutes, so each knows what the other has seen. The Protagonist and Ives fight their way to the hypocentre to recover the Algorithm before it is buried. Volkov traps them behind a locked gate, until a dead soldier on the other side, moving backward in time, rises, unlocks it and dies in their place. He has the orange trinket on his bag. They escape with the Algorithm moments before the explosion. In Vietnam, Kat keeps Sator alive until the Algorithm is safe, then kills him.

What happens: after the battle, the Protagonist, Neil and Ives split the Algorithm into three parts, each to hide one where no one will find it. The Protagonist notices the orange trinket on Neil's bag and realises Neil is the soldier who died at the gate. Neil explains that for him, this is not the start of their friendship but the end. Years in the Protagonist's future, the Protagonist recruited Neil to Tenet, and they have worked together for a long time. Neil now goes back through a turnstile to the battle, to die opening the gate. Later, in London, Priya plans to have Kat killed to protect the secret. The Protagonist, who now understands that he is the one who founded Tenet, shoots Priya first and watches Kat and Max walk away safe.

ul: The Protagonist is Tenet's founder. In the future he builds the organisation, recruits Neil, Priya and the others, and sets up the events of the film; at the start he was walking into a plan he himself had made. The film shows this directly.

What's happened, happened. The film's time travel cannot change the past. Characters can only do what they have already done, which is why Neil goes to his death knowing it is coming. Critics often read the ending as fate seen from both directions.
Who saved the Protagonist at the opera? The masked soldier in Kyiv also carries the orange trinket, which points to Neil; the film does not say so outright.
Is Neil Kat's son Max, grown up? This is a popular fan theory. Nothing in the film confirms it, and critics treat it as speculation.

body: Why does the future attack the past? Sator says the people of the future are trying to undo the damage that has made their world dying, and see reversing time as their only way out. The film presents the Algorithm as a threat that would wipe out everyone living now, the grandfather paradox on a global scale.

ul: Fate and free will: every character acts in a loop that is already closed, yet each chooses to play their part.
Friendship: the Protagonist and Neil's partnership is lived in opposite directions, ending for one as it begins for the other.
Control and abuse: Sator's grip on Kat, through the painting and their son, is set against her final act of breaking free.
Responsibility to the future and the past: the war asks whether a dying future has the right to destroy the present to save itself.
Runtime: 150 minutes. English-language; released in August and September 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
An original screenplay by Nolan; the title is a palindrome, and a famous Latin word square containing TENET and SATOR inspires several names in the film.
Content: rated PG-13 in the US; frequent gunfire and fighting, a scene of torture and domestic abuse.
Dialogue is famously hard to hear in places, and the film's opening hour moves fast; many viewers watch it twice or with subtitles.

check.q: What does an inverted bullet do?
options: It moves backward in time, flying back into the gun
check.why: Inverted objects run backward through time, so the bullet is caught by the gun rather than fired.

check.q: Why does Sator want to trigger the Algorithm?
options: He is paid by the CIA
He wants to rule the future
He is dying of cancer and wants the world to end with him
check.why: Kat explains that Sator has terminal cancer and intends to take the world with him when he dies.

options: The Protagonist, in his own future
check.why: At the end the Protagonist realises that his future self created Tenet and recruited Neil.

faq.q: Does Neil die at the end of Tenet?
faq.a: Yes. He goes back through a turnstile to the battle at Stalsk-12 and becomes the inverted soldier who opens the gate and is killed, saving the Protagonist and Ives.

faq.q: What is the Algorithm in Tenet?
faq.a: A device in nine pieces, made in the future, that could invert the entire world's entropy. Turning it on would destroy the past, including everyone alive in the present.

faq.q: What is a temporal pincer movement?
faq.a: An operation in which one team moves forward in time and another moves backward through the same period, so the backward team can tell the forward team what is going to happen.
